title: The Phone:
title_short: The Phone · Messages for Someone Healing
length: about 100 s (about 80 s with the three lifts)
headline: A phone on a stool in Bryant Park. Strangers leave voicemails for a patient recovering from surgery.
story: A handset sits on a stool with a sign: “Hey, stranger. Leave a voice message for someone recovering from surgery.” People pick it up, hear the beep and talk to someone they will never meet. The messages go to real Watsi patients.

The spine is people who have been through it: a man in a wheelchair who is “still on the other side”, a wife whose husband survived five surgeries, a mother. Around them, the short and funny ones: ice cream, favorite food, “Hi mom”. Warm and full of life, never sad. It ends on Mackinnon thanking the patient.
do: Open on the man in the wheelchair. Top text on frame 1.
Cut with the MP3 voice. Sync each MP3 to its MOV by waveform.
Show the stool and sign once, at the “how it works” beat.
Bleep the one swear word. Keep the line.
English subtitles on Ana's Portuguese message.
dont: Never use Nick's message (MIC0028). He is our videographer.
No names from folder labels. “Headphones Dude” is not a name.
No text over the health details.
No sign or logo readable at 0:00.

tech: IMG_xxxx.MOV: 1920×1080 stored with a rotation flag, plays vertical 1080×1920, 30 fps, 2-ch camera audio. Check Premiere reads the rotation.
MIC00xx.MP3 from the recorder in the handset. This is the voice you cut with. The MOV audio is only for sync and park sound.
1080×1920 at 30 fps, same as the MOVs.
None. The MOVs are already vertical. Punch-ins are upscales: keep them at 115% or less.
Phone audio is thin. Light EQ and a little compression so every message sits at the same level. Park sound from the MOV under it, low.
Lato Bold, white, soft shadow, large. Pop word by word. No highlight box, no shading block. One line at a time. Always on screen, also in pauses. Keep the bottom 20% clear for app buttons.
H.264 MP4, 1080×1920, about 16 Mbps. One file, 9:16 only.
checklist: Read every caption against the MP3 audio.
Watsi is spelled with a capital W only. Never “WOTC”.
Every MP3 is in sync with its MOV.
The swear word is bleeped and captioned “[bleep]”.
Name supers only for people who say their name: Anissa, Ana, Mackinnon. Large, first name only, never before 0:05.
No music anywhere. Every message is at the same level.
Nick's message (MIC0028) is not in the cut.

decisions.b: The brief asks for 60–75 s. With every person it chose, the cut is about 100 s. The three “Lift” rows (tough love, blue dress, fancy jacket) take it to about 80 s. Nick decides.
End card: watsi.org, or the Who Gives close, “Tell us your story.” + watsi.org/who-gives (planned)? This cut uses the Who Gives look. Confirm.
Production Planning row 12949181905 still says Reference = Requested, owner Nick. Sonam suggested givewithjose.com on 15 Sep. A producer has to pick it.
